connection: Session 18 created IClockEntryRepository, and Session 19 compared interfaces with inheritance. App still creates the repository directly. This session creates the first service with a genuine repository dependency and supplies that dependency through its constructor.
objectives: Explain dependency direction: ClockEntryService knows IClockEntryRepository, not its concrete class.
Store an injected dependency in a private readonly field so service methods can use it after construction.
Coordinate clock-in and clock-out without exposing repository storage.
Compose ClockEntryRepository and ClockEntryService manually in Program.cs before learning a DI container.

visuals.title: Constructor injection makes the dependency visible
visuals.explanation: ClockEntryService requires IClockEntryRepository in its constructor and preserves it in a private readonly field.

visuals.title: The service points toward the contract
visuals.explanation: ClockEntryService names IClockEntryRepository; only Program.cs chooses ClockEntryRepository.

visuals.title: The service coordinates two use cases
visuals.explanation: TryClockIn rejects a second open entry. TryClockOut rejects an employee with no open entry.

visuals.title: Manual composition first
visuals.explanation: Program creates one repository instance and passes that same instance into the service. No container or lifetime terminology is needed yet.

preQuiz.prompt: Why is the injected repository stored in a class field?
options: Service methods need it after the constructor returns
preQuiz.explanation: A constructor parameter is local to the constructor; the field preserves the reference for the object's lifetime.

preQuiz.prompt: Which file should choose ClockEntryRepository as the implementation?
preQuiz.explanation: The outer composition root chooses concrete implementations.

preQuiz.prompt: Is a DI container required for constructor injection?
options: No; Program can pass the dependency with new
preQuiz.explanation: Constructor injection is the design; a container automates construction later.

concept.title: Constructor injection makes a requirement explicit
paragraphs: ClockEntryService cannot coordinate clock operations without repository access, so its constructor requires IClockEntryRepository.
The field is declared on the class because TryClockIn and TryClockOut need it after construction.

concept.title: The service coordinates; the model protects its own state
paragraphs: TryClockIn checks for an existing open entry before constructing and saving a new one.
TryClockOut locates the open entry, then asks that ClockEntry object to complete itself through the method established in your source.

concept.title: Manual composition comes before a container
paragraphs: Program.cs creates one repository and passes it to ClockEntryService. This makes object identity and shared in-memory state visible.
A DI container and Transient/Singleton lifetimes are deferred until the testing and DI layer.
concept.code:
IClockEntryRepository repository = new ClockEntryRepository();
var clockEntries = new ClockEntryService(repository);

concept.title: Architecture note — domain service versus application service
paragraphs: A domain service contains business rules that belong to the domain but do not fit naturally inside one entity. An application service coordinates a use case: retrieve data, invoke domain behavior, save changes, and return a result.

ClockEntryService is primarily an application service because it coordinates IClockEntryRepository and ClockEntry. The course keeps it in Domain to avoid adding another project during this lesson. In a larger production solution, the preferred location would commonly be PinkMachine19.TimeClock.Application/Services/ClockEntryService.cs.

lab.objective: Create ClockEntryService with one constructor-injected repository and compose it manually from App.
lab.startingCondition: Session 18 created IClockEntryRepository and ClockEntryRepository implements it. No production service or DI container exists.
lab.keyPointTitle: Constructor injection does not require a container
keyPoints: The service depends on the interface.
The private readonly field preserves the collaborator.
Program chooses and shares the concrete repository instance.
The service coordinates existing repository and model behavior rather than duplicating it.
steps: Create ClockEntryService.cs in the Domain project.
Declare a public sealed ClockEntryService class.
Declare a private readonly IClockEntryRepository field.
Create a constructor with one IClockEntryRepository parameter.
Assign the parameter to the field.
Stub TryClockIn with employeeId and clockIn parameters.
In TryClockIn, call GetOpenClockEntry for the employee.
Return false when an open entry already exists.
Construct a ClockEntry only after that check succeeds.
Save the new entry through IClockEntryRepository.
Return true.
Stub TryClockOut with employeeId and clockOut parameters.
Locate the employee's open entry.
Return false when no open entry exists.
Call the existing ClockEntry completion method on the found entry.
Return true.
Build before modifying App.
Append a Session 20 section to App/Program.cs.
Construct one ClockEntryRepository as an IClockEntryRepository variable.
Pass that same variable to ClockEntryService.
Call TryClockIn and TryClockOut for one employee and display both results.

steps.text: Run App, then build and test. Open the solution only after your attempt.
steps.code:
dotnet run --project src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.App/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.App.csproj --configuration Release
dotnet build PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln --configuration Release && dotnet test PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln --configuration Release --no-build

reveals.title: Solution
reveals.text: If your earlier ClockEntry completion method has a different name, use the method present in your source.

lab.expectedBehavior: The first clock-in and clock-out succeed, invalid repeated operations return false, and the same repository instance retains the entry across service calls.

postQuiz.prompt: What is the dependency direction inside ClockEntryService?
postQuiz.explanation: The service names the stable contract.

postQuiz.prompt: Why must Program reuse the same in-memory repository instance for clock-in and clock-out?
options: The second operation must see state saved by the first
postQuiz.explanation: Two separate in-memory repositories would own two separate Lists.

postQuiz.prompt: What is the DI container doing in this session?

reflections: Why should ClockEntryService not construct ClockEntryRepository inside its own constructor?
What does readonly prevent on the dependency field?
Which rule belongs to ClockEntry and which coordination belongs to ClockEntryService?
whatBreaks: Depending directly on ClockEntryRepository removes the substitution seam. Constructing a repository inside each method loses shared in-memory state. Keeping the dependency only as a constructor parameter makes it unavailable to later service methods.
summary: Session 20 creates the ClockEntryService required by later error and async sessions. It depends on IClockEntryRepository, stores that collaborator in a private readonly field, and is composed manually in App without premature container or lifetime configuration.
